title: Ex5 - Open: Pie chart interpretation
text:
Run the code below in a new cell:

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

url1 = "https://github.com/muratfirat78/CPP_Datasets/raw/main/company_sales_data.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(url1, sep=',')

labels = ['FaceCream', 'FaceWash', 'ToothPaste', 'Bathing soap', 'Shampoo', 'Moisturizer']
salesData = [df['facecream'].sum(), df['facewash'].sum(), df['toothpaste'].sum(),
             df['bathingsoap'].sum(), df['shampoo'].sum(), df['moisturizer'].sum()]
plt.axis('equal')
plt.pie(salesData, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%')
plt.legend(loc='lower right')
plt.title('Sales data')
plt.show()
```

Look at the pie chart of annual product sales. Which product has the largest share? What is a limitation of a pie chart compared to a bar chart for this data?
answer: Bathingsoap has the largest share. A limitation of pie charts is that small differences between slices are hard to compare accurately. The solution uses df['column'].sum() per product and plt.pie() with autopct for percentages.
